sections.title: Expressions with COME
sections.content:
Fixed phrases using COME:
• come to terms with — accept a difficult situation. She's slowly coming to terms with the loss.
• come to a conclusion — reach a decision. After much debate, we came to a conclusion.
• come into effect — begin to apply. The new law comes into effect next month.
• come across — find by chance. I came across an interesting article online.
• come in handy — be useful at some point. That extra training might come in handy later.

sections.title: Expressions with GO
sections.content:
Fixed phrases using GO:
• go to great lengths — make a lot of effort. She went to great lengths to prepare for the interview.
• go without saying — be obvious. It goes without saying that hard work pays off.
• go through — experience something difficult. He's going through a tough time at work.
• go ahead — proceed. We've decided to go ahead with the project.
• go downhill — deteriorate. After the CEO left, things went downhill rapidly.

exercises.question: To accept a painful situation is to come to ___ with it:
exercises.explanation: Come to terms with means to accept a difficult situation.

exercises.question: If something 'goes without saying', it is:
exercises.explanation: Goes without saying means it is so obvious it doesn't need to be stated.

exercises.question: To make extraordinary effort is to go to great ___:
exercises.explanation: Go to great lengths means to try very hard to achieve something.

exercises.question: When a law begins to apply, it comes into:
exercises.explanation: Come into effect means to start being enforced or applied.

exercises.question: Finding something by chance is to come ___:
exercises.explanation: Come across means to find or encounter by chance.

exercises.question: When a situation gets worse, it goes:
exercises.explanation: Go downhill means to deteriorate or get worse.

exercises.question: Something useful in the future might come in:
exercises.explanation: Come in handy means to turn out to be useful when needed.

exercises.question: To experience a difficult period is to go ___:
exercises.explanation: Go through means to experience a difficult or unpleasant situation.
